transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time today. I'm sure it's probably just normal work stress, but... well, I've been losing these chunks of time lately. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, actually, because it sounds so silly out loud. But I just have this habit where I end up re-reading my emails and texts over and over, or... or reopening computer folders just to check them again. And before I leave the house or start my work for the day, I sort of get stuck mentally replaying conversations I've had. 

I guess I'm just trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake. I just want to be thorough and do a good job, you know? Is that... does that make sense? I'm sure a lot of people do things like that, right?
Do you find yourself having thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Um... yes, I suppose I do. But, you know, I think it's mostly just because I care a lot about doing the right thing. Am I making sense? 

Like, even when I'm right in the middle of something that needs my full attention—say I'm trying to work through a computer system design for my job, or... or prepare a lesson—this thought just sort of... barges in. It's usually something personal and, honestly, a bit embarrassing to get so hung up on. I'll start worrying that I might have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I somehow mishandled some important family photos... or just this heavy feeling that I've let someone in the community down. 

I try to stop thinking about it, I really do, because I know I've already been over it in my head. But I just can't seem to let it pass. I'm sure you hear that all the time from people who just want to be conscientious, right? It's probably a pretty common thing to worry about... isn't it?
Do you feel like you need to do certain things over and over, like checking or cleaning, to feel okay?

Um, yes, I suppose so. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but... that's actually exactly why I decided to come in today. 

I don't really do the cleaning thing—my place is pretty normal, I think. But the checking... yeah. Like I was trying to say earlier, I just keep losing these big chunks of time because I feel like I have to re-read my emails and texts over and over. Or I'll keep reopening the same computer folders at work, just to look at them one more time. And before I can even leave the house or start my work, I have to mentally replay those conversations in my head. 

I just do it until I feel... okay, I guess. Until I can prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake somewhere. I know it probably sounds a little excessive when I describe it like that, but I really just want to make sure I'm doing things right and being a good employee. That's a pretty normal way to handle stress, don't you think? Is that the kind of thing you meant?
Do you feel like these habits of checking and replaying conversations are interfering with your daily life or causing you a lot of distress?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's completely interfering, you know? I'm still functioning and everything. I try very hard to keep it all together. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has caused a few hiccups lately. 

Just because I'm trying to be so thorough, my work has slowed down a bit. I've actually missed a couple of design milestones, which really isn't like me at all. And... well, I've had to postpone some mentoring sessions at the office that I usually handle pretty reliably. I'm sure every programmer gets a little behind schedule sometimes though, right? It's probably just normal burnout.

But the part that really... the part I feel most embarrassed to admit is about this youth coding workshop I volunteer for. It means a lot to me, but recently I was so stuck on checking things before I left the house that I ended up being late and just... completely unprepared for it. I felt terrible. I really pride myself on being dependable, you know? I just need to figure out how to manage my time a bit better so I don't let people down. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I don't sound completely incompetent saying all this.
How much distress do these habits of checking and replaying conversations cause you?

Well, um... distress might be a little bit of a strong word. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, you know? I mean, I'm not falling apart or anything like that. 

It's... it's just a little frustrating sometimes. Nobody likes feeling like they're wasting their own time. But I handle it okay, I think! It just gets a bit exhausting, having to... to go over things so much. It's sort of like working a double shift in my head, I guess. But I'm sure most people feel a little overwhelmed when they just want to do a good job, right? 

I just really don't want you to think I'm overreacting to normal everyday pressures. I know everyone has stress. Am I... am I answering your question the right way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
Do you feel a strong urge to perform specific physical actions, like tapping or touching things, as part of your daily routine?

No, no, I don't really do anything like that. I mean, I might tap my pen on the desk if I'm thinking really hard about a piece of code, but that's just normal fidgeting, right? I don't feel like I *have* to do it or anything. 

I don't have to touch doorframes or count things or anything physical like that. It's really all just... up here, in my head, or on the screen. I hope that's okay? I mean, I hope that's a normal way to answer that. I just don't want to make you think things are worse than they are, because honestly, physically, I'm just a regular guy. Does that make sense?
Would you say that these habits of checking and replaying conversations are causing you more than just a little frustration?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, "more than a little frustration" sounds so... so serious, you know? I really don't want to come across like I'm whining or that I can't handle my own life. I try to stay positive about it. 

But... I suppose, if I'm really thinking about it... it is a bit more than just a passing annoyance. It can be pretty draining. Especially when I'm trying to sleep and my brain just won't shut off, or when I realize I've spent an hour reviewing an email that was perfectly fine to begin with. It's... it's definitely tiring. 

I just... I really hope you don't think I'm making a mountain out of a molehill here. I know there are people dealing with much worse things. I just want to be helpful and give you the right picture. Is that... does that answer what you were asking? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can without blowing things out of proportion.
Are there things or situations that you avoid because of these repetitive thoughts or habits?

Oh, um... avoid things? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still do everything I'm supposed to do. I still log on for work every day, I still go to all my meetings, write my code... I would never want to let my team down or, you know, shirk my responsibilities just because I'm feeling a little bogged down in my own head. 

I really pride myself on being reliable, so I just kind of push through it. Even if it takes me a little longer to double-check an email or review a project, I still do it. I'm not hiding from life or staying away from people or anything like that. I really try to just keep functioning like a normal, dependable guy. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I figure as long as I'm not running away from my work, I'm doing okay. Is that... does that help answer what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends, family, or colleagues due to your habits of checking and replaying conversations?

Oh, um... well, my colleagues are really wonderful, very understanding people. I try so hard not to let any of this affect them, because I really value those relationships. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has bled into my professional life a little bit lately. 

I mean, I'm still working hard, but my pace has slowed down just enough that I've... well, I've missed a couple of design milestones. And I've actually had to postpone some mentoring sessions with the junior devs, which is something I usually handle really reliably. I just didn't want to sit down with them while my head was so cluttered, you know? 

And... well, there was also this youth coding workshop I volunteer for. It really matters to me, but recently I ended up being late and totally unprepared for it because I was stuck reviewing things before I left the house. I was pretty embarrassed about that, to be honest. I felt awful letting those kids down. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee or a bad mentor. I'm really trying my best to catch up and fix it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you experienced any significant problems at work or in your personal relationships as a direct result of these habits and thoughts?

Um... I think... I mean, I sort of just mentioned the work stuff, with the milestones and the mentoring. But beyond that? Like, significant problems? I really don't think so. 

I mean, "significant" is a pretty strong word, right? I'd like to think I'm still a good friend and a good person to be around. I try really, really hard to keep all this... this mental clutter to myself so it doesn't bother anyone else. I don't want to be a burden or have people think I'm, you know, difficult to deal with. 

So, no, I wouldn't say there are any major disasters or anything like that. Just the few hiccups at work I mentioned, which I'm already trying to smooth over. I really hope that makes sense? I'm just trying to make sure I'm answering you correctly without making it sound like my whole life is falling apart, because it's really not. Am I... am I giving you the right kind of answers here?
Are there any specific situations or activities that you tend to avoid because of your need to check or replay conversations?

Oh, um... I think I might have touched on this a little bit earlier, but... no, not really. Even with the... you know, the need to go over conversations in my head again and again, I really don't avoid things. 

I mean, if there's a team lunch or a meeting, or even just chatting with someone in the breakroom, I still do it. I might be a little quieter than usual if my mind is sort of... stuck on a loop, or I might take a second longer to reply, but I definitely still participate. 

I really wouldn't want to be the kind of person who just withdraws from everyone. That would feel like letting people down, and I try very hard to be present and engaged. So I just kind of push through the mental noise and show up anyway. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know. Am I still on the right track with these answers?
Do you feel like you have to repeat certain words or phrases to yourself as part of your daily thoughts?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely get stuck replaying things people have said to me, like I mentioned before, but I don't have, like... a specific word or phrase that I have to say over and over to myself. 

I try to keep my thoughts pretty focused on, you know, just trying to figure out if I said the right thing or if I offended someone. I don't have any sort of... chanting or anything like that going on in my head. I'd like to think my thoughts are mostly pretty normal, just maybe a bit more... thorough? 

I hope that's an okay answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture. I'm not trying to hide anything, I just honestly don't think I do that specific thing. Is that helpful?
Do you feel like you have to think about certain things in a specific way, like counting or repeating certain steps in your head?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I do anything like counting or... or going through steps like that. 

I mean, I definitely try to be careful and methodical in how I think things through, especially with work—you kind of have to be in my field, right? But I don't have any strict rules in my head where I have to count to a certain number or think about things in a very rigid, step-by-step way just for the sake of it. 

I really just try to make sure I'm being thorough and considerate. I wouldn't want you to think my mind is entirely consumed by, like, weird rituals or anything. I'm just trying to be a conscientious person, you know? 

I hope that answers what you're asking? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression about how my mind works. Does that sound like a normal way to explain it?
Would you say that the frustration you experience from these habits is more than just a minor annoyance?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it might be a little more than just a minor annoyance. I really try my best not to let it affect my day-to-day life, but... well, my work has slowed down a bit recently. I've actually missed a couple of design milestones, which isn't like me at all. And I've had to postpone some mentoring sessions with the junior developers that I usually handle without any issues. I really hate letting them down.

And, um... this is actually a little hard to admit, but... I also volunteer for a youth coding workshop, and recently I showed up late and completely unprepared because I was just so caught up in my head. It was really embarrassing for me, because that program matters a lot to me and I always want to set a good example for the kids. 

I hope you don't think I'm just completely dropping the ball everywhere. I really am trying my hardest to stay on top of my responsibilities, I just... get a little tangled up sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I shared that, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like you have to mentally replay conversations or events in a specific order or until you reach a certain conclusion?

Well, um... I guess that kind of touches on why I actually decided to come in. I wouldn't say I do it in a specific order, exactly, but... I do find myself mentally replaying conversations quite a bit. Especially before I leave the house or right before I start my work day. 

It's just... I guess I'm trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some sort of serious mistake, you know? Like I said, I just want to be thorough. But it's gotten to the point where I'm losing chunks of time doing it. And it's not just conversations in my head, I... I also find myself re-reading emails and texts a lot. Sometimes I'll even reopen folders on my computer just to check things again. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly, and I really try not to let it take over, but... it does eat up more time than I'd like to admit. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely unhinged. I'm just trying to be really careful and make sure everything is right. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope that's an okay answer.
Do you feel like you have to think about certain things in a very precise or specific way to feel okay?

Um, no, I don't think so. I feel like that might be a little bit like what you were asking earlier? I really don't have a... a precise or specific formula I have to follow in my head just to feel okay. 

I mean, I like to be logical and clear, especially since my background is in computers, but it's not like I have this rigid mental rule I have to follow to calm down or anything. It's really just the replaying and the checking that I mentioned, just to be absolutely sure I didn't make a careless mistake. 

I hope I'm understanding your question correctly? I certainly don't want to mislead you or give you the wrong idea. Am I answering that the way you need me to?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't use the word 'significant' distress. And definitely not most of the time. I mean, it's a little annoying, sure, like I mentioned with the work stuff, but I really do manage it pretty well overall.

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture and not making it sound worse than it actually is. Am I explaining that okay for you?

Well, um... I really try not to let it get to that point. I want to be someone people can count on, you know? But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it has impacted things a little bit lately.

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really value my relationships, and I try to be a good friend and, you know, a supportive person to the people in my life. I don't think my... my habits have ever stopped me from getting close to people or keeping friends.

I wouldn't want anyone to feel like they aren't important to me. My marriage is good, and I have good friends. I really hope I'm being clear about that? I wouldn't want you to think I'm isolated or pushing people away, because I'm definitely not. Does that answer your question okay?
Have you felt like your habits of checking and replaying conversations have significantly impacted your ability to function at work or in your personal life?

Well, um... I guess it goes back to what I was mentioning just a little bit ago. I really hesitate to use the word 'significantly,' because I am still doing my job and, you know, living my life. I really don't want to make it sound like I'm completely unable to function or just dropping the ball everywhere. 

But... yes, if I'm being completely open with you, it has caused some issues. Like I was saying earlier, my work has slowed down enough recently that I missed those design milestones.
